\section[disculparse]{disculparse — to apologise}

\label{lesson:ES-C510-disculparse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for hope, then the Spanish for the agreement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: disculparse}
\textbf{disculparse} — \textquotedblleft{}to apologise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se disculpó por llegar tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He apologised for arriving late.}
\end{quote}

It goes with \emph{por}: \emph{disculparse por algo}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disculparse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{disculparse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{disculparse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for hope, then the Spanish for the agreement, then say \emph{disculparse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does disculparse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To apologise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[fiarse]{fiarse — to trust}

\label{lesson:ES-C510-fiarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the agreement, then the Spanish for to apologise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fiarse}
\textbf{fiarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No me fío de él.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not trust him.}
\end{quote}

It goes with \emph{de}: \emph{fiarse de alguien}. Note the accent in \emph{me fío}. In much of Latin America, \emph{confiar en} is more common.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fiarse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{fiarse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the agreement, then the Spanish for to apologise, then say \emph{fiarse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does fiarse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To trust\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pelear]{pelear — to fight, to argue}

\label{lesson:ES-C510-pelear}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to apologise, then the Spanish for to trust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: pelear}
\textbf{pelear} — \textquotedblleft{}to fight, to argue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los hermanos pelean por todo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The brothers fight about everything.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pelearse con alguien} — to fall out with someone.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
